dedupe_keys.name: transit costs project rolling stock costs database metro commuter emu and light rail orders

description: The Transit Costs Project's rolling stock costs database is the first version of a companion to its urban rail construction costs database, covering the procurement costs of metro trains, commuter rail electric multiple units (EMUs) and some light rail vehicles. Coverage: orders from three largely separate supply chains, the Chinese (mostly metros and a few 160 to 200 km/h commuter trains), the European (streetcars and light rail, metros and commuter trains) and the North American (light rail, metros and some commuter EMUs), with technical data, the vendor for each order and seat capacity where available. The main metric is purchase cost per metre of train length in 2023 PPP dollars: about $92,141 per metre for Chinese metros, $150,641 in Continental Europe (which the authors think biased upward by incompleteness, expecting about $130,000) and $152,602 in the US, dominated by New York orders. Format and access: a Google Sheets table linked from the page. Licence and cost: free to view; no licence stated. Caveats: little Japanese and Korean data so far, and the European sample is incomplete. The cost per metre and vendor data can set fleet expansion and replacement costs in transit capacity planning and supply chain models. It relates to the National Transit Database and MTA open data in the catalogue.
